conventions: bpp = Mbps*1e6/(W*H*fps) of the recorded file resolution; fixed = codecs whose bitrate does not scale with resolution/fps choice

cameras.name: Nikon Z9
cameras.notes: Reference Guide incl. "C" firmware 5.30 additions. Frame-rate labels map to actual rates per Nikon (120p=119.88, 60p=59.94, 30p=29.97, 24p=23.976). ProRes RAW HQ 12-bit is supported internally (FX 4128×2322 up to 60p, DX 5392×3032 up to 30p, 2.3× 3840×2160 50/60p) but neither Nikon nor Apple publishes a numeric data rate (Apple: RAW HQ "generally between ProRes 422 HQ and 4444") — omitted (gap).

codecs.name: N-RAW 12-bit (NEV) High quality
codecs.ref: Nikon Nikon Z9 Reference Guide, 'Video Frame Size and Rate Options' > Bit Rate table (N-RAW 12-bit (NEV) High quality): 'Approx.' Mbps per frame size/rate; rates[] are those figures (fps = actual rate per Nikon footnote, e.g. 30p = 29.97), bpp = Mbps*1e6/(W*H*fps); codec-level bpp = median. A companion MP4 (~28-120 Mbps) is also recorded for playback and is not included.
